To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the α1 and β2 subunits of GABA(A) receptors are crucial for mediating the sedative effects of different classes of drugs, and that the α1-selectivity of a drug is not a good indicator of its hypnotic efficacy.
the sedative and hypnotics actions of different drugs are mediated via the GABAA receptors.
deletion of α1 or β subunit of the GABAR complex produces a strong and specific reduction in sedative/hypotonic effects of drugs that target this receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms of drug action at the GABAA receptors in the brain and the role of the α1 and β2 subunit of GABAR in mediating sedative drug actions.
the molecular and genetic bases of the actions of drugs of addiction and abuse.
understanding of the molecular basis of sedative drug action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sedative/hyp-notic effect of drugs is dependent on GABA and its receptors and is mediated through a GABAA receptor subunit complex.
the GABA(A) receptors are a major site of action for sedative and hypnotics, including benzodiazepines and barbiturates, and that these effects are mediated by the alpha1 and beta2 subunits.
the α1 subunit of the GABAR plays an important role in the actions of sedative/hypnosis, and that the β2 subunit is also important for this function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAR is the major site of action of sedative and hypnotics and that the α1 and β2 subunits are important in the action of many of these drugs.
the α1 and β2 subunits of GABAAR are important in mediating the sedative effects of benzodiazepines and GABAAR agonists.
the GABARs are the molecular target for the action of hypnotic drugs, but the subunit composition of the receptors may determine the selectivity of the action of different drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two predominant subunits of GABAAR are essential for sedative drug action, and that the GABAAR is a key target for sedative/hypnosis.
the GABARs containing α1 or β1 subunits are the main molecular targets of the sedative drugs in the brain.
GABAA receptors containing either the α1- or β2-subunit are important targets for sedative/hypnoic drug action.
